@graph.name: Engage Marin 101
@graph.abstract: Learn how County teams use Engage Marin to ask residents a question and share what they learned.

@graph.name: Overview
@graph.marin:text: Engage Marin is the County of Marin’s online platform for community input. It gives people a simple way to share ideas and give feedback. That feedback helps shape County decisions. You can ask one question. You can also bring several related questions together in a campaign. Every engagement follows the same eight steps. They are plan, create, partner, launch, monitor, organize, update, and close. Your team brings the topic and community knowledge. The Engage Marin team helps you plan, launch, and manage the conversation.

@graph.name: Why it matters
marin:items: You reach more people and hear different views.
You learn what matters to the community.
People get one simple place to share ideas and give feedback.
Their feedback helps shape County decisions.
People know they were heard, even if the County cannot act on every idea.

@graph.name: Problem
@graph.marin:text: County channels may not reach everyone. Some people may never hear about a chance to share ideas. Others share ideas and never learn what happened.

@graph.name: Solution
@graph.marin:text: Start with three questions: What do you want to learn? Who do you want to hear from? How will you use their feedback? Then follow the eight steps, work with community partners early, and close with a recap that says what you heard and what happens next.

@graph.name: User stories
marin:items: As a project lead, I want a clear question and plan, so I can invite useful ideas.
As a team member, I want to work with community partners early, so I can reach more people.
As a project lead, I want to share what we learned, so people see how their input helped.
As a resident, I want to know what happened, so I can see how my ideas were used.

marin:items.definition: The County’s online platform where people share ideas, give feedback, and help shape decisions.
Several related questions brought together under one larger effort.
Where people share ideas, comment, and vote. It has its own page, updates, themes, and reports.
A trusted local group, such as a nonprofit, school, or neighborhood group, that helps invite people.
A group of related ideas that helps you see what people are saying across many responses.
A post that shares progress and keeps people informed while a question is open.
A page that gives people background on a question: what, why, who, when, and next steps.
A welcome post that starts the conversation and shows that someone is listening.
Telling people what you heard, what you learned, and what happens next.

marin:items.dont: Lead people toward a preferred answer.
Use jargon or internal project names.
Wait until your question is ready to publish.

marin:items.do: Focus on what people want to share.
marin:items.dont: Write about the County instead of the people taking part.

marin:items.do: Share a recap when the question closes.
marin:items.dont: Let the engagement end without explaining what happened.

@graph.name: Questions to ask
marin:items: What do we want to learn?
Who do we want to hear from?
How will we use their feedback?
Which community partners could help us reach people?
Who on our team will lead the effort and follow the conversation?
Is our question short, open, and neutral?
How will we tell people what we learned?

@graph.name: Checklist
marin:items: We know what we want to learn.
We know who we want to reach.
We have a clear question or campaign.
We have identified community partners.
We have an outreach plan.
We have an About page and a welcome post.
Someone will monitor activity and post updates.
We have a plan to share results.

@graph.name: Mantras
marin:items: Start with a question. End with an answer.
Partner early.
Listen, learn, and show how input matters.
Close the loop.
